videos.script: A reader finishes a book at Marginalia and wants the next one. The shop has sixty to offer. Which five does it show her? {{shelf}} This lesson answers that with the vectors you already know. Every book becomes a vector made from its title and its blurb. {{books}} Books whose vectors are close make a list called more like this. You will read that list critically, because the model's idea of close is not always yours. {{like}} Then a reader becomes a vector too, the average of the books she finished. {{reader}} A reader who likes two different things lands in between, and you will see what that does. {{between}} You will remove what she has read, stop one author taking over the list, and respect the shop's own rules. {{filters}} You will trade a little similarity for variety, with a single number that you choose. {{variety}} And you will meet the hardest case: a reader the shop knows nothing about. {{coldstart}}
